OpenAI has expanded its GPT-6 lineup with two new models—GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna—delivering significant price reductions while maintaining strong performance across professional work, coding, and computer use tasks.

The new models represent OpenAI's effort to make frontier AI more accessible. GPT-6 Sol is positioned as the cost-efficient alternative to the flagship GPT-6 Astra, while GPT-6 Luna targets high-volume, lower-complexity workloads.

## Pricing That Changes the Game

The pricing overhaul slashes costs by 50% compared to GPT-5.6 promotional rates. GPT-6 Sol now costs $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, down from $4 and $20 respectively. GPT-6 Luna drops to $0.10 input and $0.50 output, making it one of the most affordable frontier-tier options available.

"We trained GPT-6 Sol and Luna with similar methods as GPT-6 Astra, bringing the advances behind Astra's state-of-the-art performance in professional work, factuality, coding, computer use, and alignment to faster, more affordable models," OpenAI stated in the announcement.

## Benchmark Performance

The new models demonstrate impressive efficiency gains. On AutomationBench, which tests business workflows across 47 tools spanning sales, marketing, operations, and finance, GPT-6 Sol at xhigh effort outperforms Claude Opus 5 at max effort at just 9% of the cost.

On coding tasks measured by DeepSWE v1.1, GPT-6 Sol at max effort scores 68.8%—within 1.1 percentage points of Claude Fable 5's highest score—at approximately 80% lower cost per task. GPT-6 Luna achieves 66.6%, comparable to Claude Opus 5 and Fable 5 at medium effort.

For computer use on OSWorld 2.0, GPT-6 Sol at xhigh effort reaches 60.5%, matching Claude Opus 5 at medium effort at roughly 80% lower cost.

## Improved Collaboration Style

Both models inherit GPT-6 Astra's communication improvements, offering clearer responses, less jargon, and more concise answers without losing substance. The models are now available in ChatGPT Work, Codex, and the OpenAI API.
